title: Circular Measure Module 3 Lesson 1: External Tangents & Tangent Kites custom practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, values and combinations are original; mapped Cambridge evidence informs scope and assessment structure only.

parts.prompt: Tangents $TA$ and $TB$ are drawn from an external point $T$ to touch a circle of radius $9\text{ cm}$ at $A$ and $B$. Given that the central angle $\angle AOB = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}\text{ radians}$, find the exact length of the tangent $TA$.
A tangent from a point $T$ touches a circle of radius $5\text{ cm}$ at $A$. The length of the tangent $TA$ is $12\text{ cm}$. Find the exact distance from $T$ to the centre $O$ of the circle.

Tangents $TA$ and $TB$ touch a circle of radius $6\text{ cm}$ at $A$ and $B$. The angle $\angle AOT$ between radius $OA$ and the line of centres $OT$ is $\dfrac{\pi}{4}\text{ radians}$. Find the exact area of the kite $OATB$.

Tangents from an external point $T$ touch a circle of radius $6\text{ cm}$ at $A$ and $B$, with $\angle AOT = \dfrac{\pi}{3}\text{ radians}$. Find the exact area of the region enclosed by the tangents $TA, TB$ and the minor arc $AB$.

Tangents $TA$ and $TB$ touch a circle of radius $4\text{ cm}$ at $A$ and $B$, and $\angle AOT = \dfrac{\pi}{3}\text{ radians}$. Find the exact perimeter of the region enclosed by $TA, TB$ and the minor arc $AB$.

Tangents from $T$ touch a circle of radius $3\text{ cm}$ at $A$ and $B$. The length of each tangent is $\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}$. Find the exact angle $\angle AOB$ subtended at the centre of the circle in terms of $\pi$.
Tangents from $T$ touch a circle of radius $6\text{ cm}$. Half the central angle between radii to the contacts is $0.5\text{ radians}$. Find one tangent length.
